1. Load the London borough data and the borough‐neighbour list into pandas DataFrames.  
2. Check both DataFrames for missing values; if any are found, drop those borough rows entirely (and their corresponding entries in the neighbour list) so that Gas, Waste, and adjacency all remain defined.  
3. From the neighbour list, construct a binary spatial weight matrix W (33×33) where W[i,j]=1 if i and j are neighbors, 0 otherwise; row‐standardize W so each row sums to 1.  
4. Extract the Gas vector G and Waste vector H (length 33) and standardize each to zero mean and unit variance.  
5. Compute Lee’s L bivariate spatial correlation statistic:  
   L_obs = (Gᵀ W H) / sum of all W entries.  
6. Perform a permutation test with at least 500 random shuffles: for each shuffle k, randomly permute H across boroughs to get H_k, compute L_k = (Gᵀ W H_k)/sum W; collect the L_k distribution.  
7. Calculate the two‐sided p‐value as the proportion of |L_k| ≥ |L_obs| over all permutations.  
8. Compare p to α=0.05:  
   • If p<0.05 and L_obs>0 ⇒ POSITIVE spatial association  
   • If p<0.05 and L_obs<0 ⇒ NEGATIVE spatial association  
   • Otherwise ⇒ NOT SIGNIFICANT

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load data
data_path = "chunks_csv/bivariate/bivariate_2021_gas_waste.csv"
adj_path = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(data_path, index_col=None)
df_adj = pd.read_csv(adj_path, index_col=None)

# Drop missing values
df = df.dropna(subset=["borough", "Gas_value", "Waste_value"])
boroughs = sorted(df["borough"].unique())
n = len(boroughs)

# Filter adjacency to only include these boroughs
df_adj = df_adj[df_adj["borough"].isin(boroughs) & df_adj["neighbor"].isin(boroughs)]

# Build index mapping
idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

# Build adjacency matrix
W = np.zeros((n, n), dtype=float)
for _, row in df_adj.iterrows():
    i = idx[row["borough"]]
    j = idx[row["neighbor"]]
    W[i, j] = 1
    W[j, i] = 1  # ensure symmetry

# Row-standardize W
row_sums = W.sum(axis=1)
W_norm = np.divide(W, row_sums[:, None], where=row_sums[:, None] != 0)
sum_W = W_norm.sum()

# Extract and standardize variables
df = df.set_index("borough").loc[boroughs]
G = df["Gas_value"].values
H = df["Waste_value"].values
G_std = (G - G.mean()) / np.std(G)
H_std = (H - H.mean()) / np.std(H)

# Observed Lee's L
L_obs = (G_std @ W_norm @ H_std) / sum_W

# Permutation test
np.random.seed(0)
n_perm = 500
L_perms = np.zeros(n_perm)
for k in range(n_perm):
    Hp = np.random.permutation(H_std)
    L_perms[k] = (G_std @ W_norm @ Hp) / sum_W

# Two-sided p-value
p_value = np.mean(np.abs(L_perms) >= abs(L_obs))

# Determine verdict
if p_value < 0.05:
    verdict = "POSITIVE" if L_obs > 0 else "NEGATIVE"
else:
    verdict = "NOT SIGNIFICANT"

# Output results
print(f"data_points_used = {n}")
print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {verdict} (test statistic = {L_obs}, p = {p_value})")
